title: First iteration of my 3d space RTS
author: _Fauxpaw
selftext:
GHOST TRACK is a game that plays with delays in receiving information. You are an Operational Intel officer in control of a battlefleet.

This is very much the first iteration (*not even sound yet, sorry for the silent reel*). One vertical slice is playable and the first Milestone is almost complete. Ship cameras, an expanded Alert Queue and rudimentary sounds are coming up next.

To keep the game from turning into pure spaghetti, Claude developed a clean simulation vs UI split: \`rules/\` has zero rendering or UI code, so the game can run headless and be written out as text for an AI to play it. \`screen/\`, the part for humans, is drawn on top.

Most of the workflow derives from using Matt Pocock's skills, which have been an organizational godsend and I can't recommend them enough. Keeping a decision record, supplied by Claude question cards, has been hugely important - along with a weekly automation to check consistency and ensure my decisions are being maintained. Oh, right, and we use Godot, which is awesome.

Labs [like this](https://claude.ai/artifact/Pi1T1J6uvGnmhB4zGPYPxe) have been *integral* to making sure myself and Claude both have a shared understanding of the spatial language of the game.

comments.author: LastingDynamicsGames
comments.body: The headless rules/ split pays off twice in a game like this, because the thing you most need to tune is the gap between what is true and what the player believes. If the sim logs both every tick (actual ship positions vs. the tracks built from the captains' reports), you get a number for "how wrong is my picture right now" and can tune report frequency, sensor noise and delay against it instead of by feel. The same log makes a great after-action screen: replay the battle with the true positions overlaid on the ghosts you were acting on. One UI thing worth deciding early is how a report's age is shown, since a three-second-old contact and a forty-second-old one shouldn't look the same on the console. Do captains report on a timer, or when something changes?
